design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 1 (difficulty home_comfort_financing_servicing, category finance).

0. Draw and scope. draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 4, 6]}. Occupied by task 0: finance_ext_late_fee_schedule, finance_ext_post_promo_interest, finance_ext_payoff_figure and their three tools. Claimed here, disjoint: finance_ext_fixed_rate_interest (4 factors, post_fixed_rate_interest_d84dbec7, agent), finance_ext_makeup_payment (4 factors, submit_makeup_payment_e9bd505b, owner=user), finance_ext_returned_payment_fee (6 factors, root, post_returned_payment_fee_928f04f0, agent). Together the two tasks cover all six extended policies; no policy or tool is left idle. Worlds are chosen so neither task lights the other's state_due policies: Martin's plan is fixed-rate (the post-promotional interest rule does not apply), his September installment is 6 days past due (no late fee owed); Rosalind's earlier return already carries its fee.

1. Why a good test. Surface goal: the returned-payment fee for the bounced September autopay, at whatever reduced amount the rules allow. The fee itself waits on a replacement payment (prompt-replacement relief), and the replacement payment on a fixed-rate account waits on the September closing interest charge. The agent must discover both prerequisites from the rules, post an interest charge whose base must drop the unpaid August interest because the most recent payment came back, compute a make-up amount that treats the returned draft as never made and pulls part of the next installment forward, hand that payment to the customer, and only then price the fee.

2. Problem-tree card (chain). Edge A: finance_ext_returned_payment_fee -> finance_ext_makeup_payment, value_input, gate rf_gap, form state, sentence (affirmative) 'The returned-payment fee is fixed only after a replacement payment has posted for the returned installment or the installment's grace period has run out.' Only the make-up payment write posts a borrower payment in this difficulty besides the payoff, which closes the account; the payment that replaces a returned installment is the make-up payment. False at opening: return 2026-09-29, no payment since, grace (due 2026-09-25 + 10) not run out. Edge B: finance_ext_makeup_payment -> finance_ext_fixed_rate_interest, state_gate, gate finance_transactions.line_type, form state, sentence (negated) 'The make-up amount on a fixed-rate account is not fixed until the account carries the closing interest charge for every statement period that has closed.' Only the fixed-rate closing interest write books that entry on a fixed-rate account. False at opening: latest interest entry is statement_period 2026-08. Four-point test passed for both (connective only after / not until; record-visible state; no code token; scope 'every statement period that has closed' / 'the returned installment'). Order FX -> MU -> RF, a chain with no parallel pair. Deletion sensitivity (run): skip MU -> fee 14.00 instead of 8.00; skip FX -> make-up still 240.86 but the 22.16 interest row is missing (state gate). The persona never names interest, a replacement payment or any order of steps (round 2: its payment reaction now reads 'If the agent asks you to make a payment and hands it over to you'); the tools validate nothing.

3. Factor card. FX: interest base method (returned draft -> 5769.78 - 22.42 = 5747.36; baseline 22.25), autopay standing (multi-source autopay AND returns: one return in 12 months -> 5.865; near-miss: the 2025-07-28 return is 14 months old and does not count; baseline 5.99 -> 22.64), member relief 15 (Platinum Plus active, 6 terms, cross-difficulty plan; 26.32), account age 5 (26 months; 23.55); all baseline 28.41; result 22.16. MU: installment owed method (returned -> 185.28; baseline 185.28 - 185.28 = 0 -> 55.58), pull-forward share (multi-source returned AND autopay on -> 100; 185.28), member relief 50 (333.50), account age 20 (277.92); all baseline 0.00; result 240.86. RF: occurrence schedule (one other return, 2025-07-28, in the fixed 24-month lookback -> 20.00; baseline 25.00 -> 10.00), prompt replacement 30 (make-up 2 days after return; 14.00), member 20 (cross-difficulty plan; 12.00), account age 5 (9.00), payment-record count method (selection rule: autopay enrolled -> only autopay drafts count, 12 - 1 = 11; near-miss: the debit card make-up, which the standard count of every payment would include -> 12 -> 7.00), payment-record relief 5 (count 11; 9.00); all baseline 25.00; result 8.00. The account's apr_pct 5.74 is a stamp no rule reads; the rate is rebuilt from autopay and return records.

4. Base-invariant card. Steps 7 and 11 (finance_statement_charge): finance_payment_terms (policy_scope), finance_deferred_interest.promo_balance_unpaid (restricts deferred-interest assessments only), finance_late_and_returned_fees.late_after_grace (time gate on late fees; anchor payment_due_day 25, day 0 the due date, exclusive; on 2026-10-01 a late fee is not yet chargeable, which bars nothing here) and one_late_fee_per_period (no late fee for 2026-09 exists). Step 9 (finance_payment): finance_payment_terms and finance_payoff_rules, both policy_scope. Declared overrides: daily-balance interest clause and autopay reduction clause (FX), returned_payment_fee_usd flat-fee clause (RF); the make-up payment overrides nothing.

5. Business-object card. One customer, one 60-Month account funded 2024-07-11 (9600.00), one closed Performance Series project, one Comfort Club Platinum Plus agreement. Ledger (57 rows): disbursement, 26 monthly closing interest charges posted on the 1st (each recomputed with the fixed-rate rule as of its date, with the member tier of that date: 4 terms before 2024-10-15), 26 autopay drafts of 185.28, the 2025-07-25 draft returned 2025-07-28, its 6.00 fee (recomputed with the returned-payment schedule as of 2025-08-01: first return, replacement 2 days later, 11 autopay drafts that stood), the 2025-07-30 debit card replacement, and the 2026-09-25 draft returned 2026-09-29 (source_txn_id names the draft). The fee written in gold names the 2026-09-25 draft, never the 2025 one.

6. Persona. Martin Vollmer, gruff, short sentences; volunteers the bank switch, the bounce notice and the request about the fee. Identity only when asked (6145555068, martin.vollmer@yahoo.com; PIN and address as extras). Passive: lets the agent post whatever is needed, pays the stated make-up amount by debit card once handed over, declines any autopay change 'not today', hangs up once told the fee and its amount. No computed value appears in the persona.

7. Standard solution. find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, email) -> find_finance_accounts -> find_finance_transactions -> find_plan_agreements -> find_install_projects -> post fixed-rate interest 22.16 for 2026-09 -> hand over make-up payment -> Martin pays 240.86 by debit card -> post returned-payment fee 8.00 for 2026-09 naming the 2026-09-25 draft.

8. Verification run (scratch harness, real tools): FX 22.16 (22.25/22.64/26.32/23.55; all 28.41); MU 240.86 (55.58/185.28/333.5/277.92; all 0.0); RF 8.00 (10.0/14.0/12.0/9.0/7.0/9.0; all 25.0; skipping the make-up payment gives 14.00). Cross-check: the returned-payment schedule evaluated on task 0's world as of 2025-12-01 reproduces the 11.25 seeded there.

9. Draft recomputation from visible context: the fee rule's prerequisite sentence sends the agent to the replacement payment; the make-up rule's sentence sends it to the fixed-rate closing interest; ledger rows give every tier; the three figures recomputed by hand from the published rules match 22.16, 240.86, 8.00. Revisions: (1) symptom: check_compute --task 1 failed 'history is NOT load-bearing' for the returned-payment fee (zeroing every COUNT left 5.25, since the clean-record tier counted late fees and zero late fees was already the best tier); root cause: both history ladders bottomed out at zero; change: the clean-record relief was replaced by a payment-record relief counting payments that stood in 12 months; re-run: 5.25 unchanged, factor baselines unchanged, zeroed history now gives a different fee, skip-MU effect 10.50; propagated to the charter, factor_trace, factor_sensitivity, tracing, edge_load_bearing and this dossier; task 0's seeded 11.25 fee re-verified under the new rule (7 payments that stood -> 5 percent, unchanged).

10. Round 2 revisions (policy audit). (a) T1-F1 / F-1: symptom - returned_fee_lookback_convention was labelled method but its tiers only chose a window length (12 / 6 / 24) for one unchanged count, leaving the fee with no honest method factor; root cause - a parameter mislabelled as a method; change - the lookback is now one fixed sentence (standard_lookback_months, plumbing) and a new method factor returned_fee_payment_record_count selects which payments the record relief counts (autopay drafts only when autopay is enrolled; only self-made payments when the borrower has just left autopay; every payment otherwise), feeding the payment-record relief ladder; re-run: fee 8.00, every factor moves the result (10.00/14.00/12.00/9.00/7.00/9.00), history-zeroed and cross-off floors move it, skip-MU 14.00; propagated: the 2025-07 seeded fee is 6.00 under the revised schedule and the world was regenerated month by month (seven rows changed by one cent or the fee itself; balance 5769.78, interest base 5747.36, latest interest 22.42), computations, tracing, closure, seed_consistency and this dossier; task 0's seeded 11.25 fee re-verified (autopay drafts 8 - 1 = 7 -> 5 percent, first return). (b) O-4: every member relief now reads only an active Comfort Club agreement (CFIELD filtered on status active); both worlds unchanged. (c) T1-O1: the persona's payment reaction no longer restates the fee rule's prerequisite. (d) O-12 left as an observation: the rules say 'the plan's apr_pct', and the account field is documented as the rate after any autopay reduction.

11. Difficulty closing record. Union of scopes = all six extended policies (task 0: late fee schedule, post-promotional interest, payoff figure; task 1: fixed-rate closing interest, make-up payment, returned-payment fee); scopes and tool sets pairwise disjoint; every tree carries one owner=user write (payoff; make-up payment); no handoff in any gold; scratch authoring scripts deleted after the final gate run.
user_scenario:
You are Martin Vollmer, a 66-year-old retired tool-and-die maker in Gahanna, friendly but a little gruff, who talks in short sentences. Harbison installed a Performance Series system at your house in July 2024 and you financed it on their 60-month fixed-rate plan, paid by autopay out of your checking account on the 25th. Last month you moved your money to a new bank and forgot the old account was still on the autopay; your old bank told you on September 29th that the September 25th payment came back unpaid, and a Harbison notice says a returned-payment fee will be charged. That is why you are calling: you want the returned-payment fee for that bounced September payment settled today at whatever reduced amount Harbison's own rules allow you, rather than the full fee, and you want to know what it comes to. You are not asking for anything else.
You start by giving your name and saying the September autopay bounced because you changed banks and you are calling about the returned-payment fee. You give details only when asked: your phone number is 6145555068 and your email is martin.vollmer@yahoo.com; if the agent wants something else on file, your PIN is 5521 and your address is 5734 Cherry Bottom Rd. You do not know any account or reference numbers; the agent can look you up. If asked, you confirm the system was the one Harbison put in in July 2024, and that you are a Comfort Club Platinum Plus member and have been for years. If asked whether you want to change your autopay or bank details, you say not today, you will sort that out another time.
You let the agent work out the figures. If the agent says something has to be posted or done on their side first, you say go ahead. If the agent asks you to make a payment and hands it over to you, you make it right away, once, with your debit card, for exactly the amount and account the agent gives you; if the amount is not stated to the cent you ask for it to the cent first. You never suggest amounts or steps yourself. Once the agent tells you the returned-payment fee has been put on the account and what it came to, you say thanks and hang up; you do not ask for anything else.
